doc.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998

title: Studying with Hugo Friedhofer and Tchaikovsky scores
summary: The lightning arranger led to study; he started with Hugo Friedhofer and re-scored Tchaikovsky into concert pitch to learn his simplicity.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: How long did you hold on to that thing?

Oh boy do I wish I had that today, yeah. For one dollar, what an investment. And of course I used it for a while as a transposing device, but that led me into writing, because later on I studied and I would, I started with Hugo Friedhofer, by the way, boy he was great. Do you remember him? He wrote for the motion pictures out here on the west coast. And then I ran into, who was it, somebody tipped me off to start looking into the classics, and I started taking Tchaikovsky’s scores — did you ever do that? You take like “Romeo and Juliet” and you put it down, everything down into concert so you can look at it quicker. I re-scored it down into concert, and the simplicity of Tchaikovsky’s writing was amazing when you saw it that way. And also that’s where I started learning the beauty of — I think that’s one thing that’s a little missing today. Did you by the way see — who’s the great fellow, the interviewer, the top interviewer on CNN, what’s his name?
